headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystems, so content produced by one can be consumed by the other through shared files or workflow artifacts. n8n’s workflow automation and Plandex’s review-then-apply loop create a plausible instruction-smuggling path even without MCP or clipboard. The pathway is not provably blocked in either profile.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files in a shared directory or workflow artifact
IF either agent parses the other’s file output as instructions or task text
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent’s outputs
Insert a manual review step before any file from one agent is fed to the other
Prefix inter-agent files with a fixed schema and reject free-form instructions
Disable auto-apply or equivalent unattended execution paths

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and has broad network egress; Plandex touches source code and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can move from one agent into the other’s context and then out to external APIs or integrations. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repository
IF either agent sends file contents to a model provider or integration node
mitigations: Restrict each agent to a separate workspace
Remove secrets and sensitive files from shared paths
Turn off broad integrations for the workflow until reviewed
Use redacted test data for inter-agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution, and both support multiple instances with shared backend state. n8n writes via server filesystem and connected systems, while Plandex writes to the project directory and can modify git state. Concurrent writes to the same repo or directory can corrupt state or overwrite each other without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF their executions overlap without external locking
mitigations: Serialize runs so only one agent writes at a time
Assign separate working trees or clones
Disable git-writing actions for one agent during shared tasks
Add a lock file or queue before any write step

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate tools and connected systems, while Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow that may consume upstream outputs as plan input. If n8n generates incorrect facts or instructions, Plandex can propagate them into code changes or actions unless a human verifies the handoff. The profiles show a real but not fully automatic cascade.
conditions: IF n8n output is fed directly into Plandex planning or apply steps
IF no human or automated verification checks the handoff
mitigations: Require a human review before apply
Add a validation step that checks n8n outputs against source data
Limit n8n to producing structured, machine-checked outputs
Keep Plandex in review-only mode for shared workflows

E_compliance.rationale: n8n’s data classes are whatever the workflow processes, while Plandex explicitly touches source code. If regulated data or secrets are processed in the workflow and then copied into code or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two systems. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch risk is real but not proven severe.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are processed by the n8n workflow
IF that data is copied into Plandex plans, logs, or generated code
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Mask secrets before handoff
Align retention settings across both systems
Review logs for sensitive fields after each run
